description: A one-person mission control bridging systems engineering and interactive game design to train the next generation of astronauts.
summary:
The "Junior Astronaut" project is an interactive lunar outpost simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, designed with a target audience of children ages 7–12. The game immerses players in managing a lunar South Pole base at Shackleton Crater, where they must carefully balance core operational resources such as power, life support oxygen, and hydroponic food.

To maximize educational value, the application enforces strict engineering trade-offs where every decision involves a genuine cost, such as balancing active water-wall and electromagnetic shielding against available battery power. Furthermore, the simulator grounds its mechanics in authentic space science by incorporating real-world data and references from NASA's DONKI space weather alerts, RadLab BLEO radiation baselines, and OSDR biological repositories.
details: Avengers Assemble is a browser-based 3D space survival game for kids ages 7–12 where players run a 7-Sol outpost on the Moon or Mars, balancing power, oxygen, hydroponic food, radiation shielding, and Earth radio delays under strict "no free lunch" trade-offs while driving a 3D rover and sheltering from solar flares. Requiring zero downloads on laptops or phones, it benefits young learners by turning intimidating aerospace science into hands-on play, aiming to spark STEM curiosity and public understanding of deep-space survival. Built with Python, Streamlit, Three.js, HTML5/CSS/JavaScript, and Web Audio API, it is grounded in real NASA DONKI space weather feeds, NASA OSDR (OSD-137, OSD-767, OSD-895), RadLab, and the CSA Food Production Toolkit. The project creatively blends unlockable Avengers commanders—each with unique 3D shields, rover driving, and fun emotes—with real Moon and Mars physics, while prioritizing age-friendly clarity, cross-device controls, replayability, and clear data attribution.
